attachments.name: medical_plan.txt
attachments.text:
Medical cover for the Clocktower Charity Run Half Marathon, Sunday 4 July 2027

From Fatima Haddad, Race Director, Clocktower Merchants' Guild

The race is a half marathon with 250 runners and starts at 09:00. An ambulance from St. Luke Ambulance Brigade is on site for the race; the paperwork is attached.

First aid
We'll have 3 first aid posts, at the start, the finish and halfway, with 8 trained first aiders between them, so nobody on the course is more than about a kilometre and a half from help. We also have two first aiders on bikes, carrying defibrillators.

Heat, cold and water
We always tell runners to dress sensibly for the weather and to keep drinking, and it's all in the email we send them the week before. We'll be watching the forecast, and people here are used to all sorts of weather.

If someone needs hospital
The nearest emergency department is at St. Brigid's Hospital, 4 km from the finish. We've walked the route out from the pick-up point at the old mill car park with the first aiders, and we've told the hospital the date and how many are coming.

Staying in touch
Everyone at a post and both bike first aiders has a radio on our medical channel, with phones as backup. Calls for an ambulance go through our medical lead, who tells the crew which barrier to come to.

Who's responsible
I take overall responsibility as organiser, along with the rest of the committee. We all care a great deal about our runners and would never let anyone come to harm.

attachments.name: race_plan.txt
attachments.text:
Clocktower Charity Run Half Marathon: how the race will work

Prepared by Fatima Haddad (Race Director), Clocktower Merchants' Guild. Last updated 12 May 2027.

This is our plan for race day, Sunday 4 July 2027. We expect 250 runners over half marathon (21 km). Numbers can be collected from the old mill car park from an hour before we go at 09:00, and we aim to have the last finisher home by 12:30.

Happily we are off-road the whole way. We use the Old Mill Trail and then the Reservoir Walk, so no streets need closing at all. We finish at the rowing club.

A word on the path. The Old Mill Trail is about 10 metres across with open ground beside it, and the Reservoir Walk is 9 metres and runs through the middle of the park, so there's lots of room to overtake. We start on the grass in a wide line.

Our club has put on races for some years now and we keep to the same simple format: chip timing, water on the course, and a hot drink at the end. Results go up on our website the same evening.
